requirement_text: We do not accept LanguageCert for entry to our courses
limitations: Page states policy version 1.0, approved by QSC in March 2025.
researcher_notes: EXCLUSION OF AN ENTIRE TEST PROVIDER, and it cuts directly across this corpus: Bath (REQ-9025 group), Exeter (Profile E) and TU Dublin (REQ-9412) all accept LanguageCert with published thresholds; Nottingham refuses it outright. A student choosing which English test to sit is choosing which universities they can apply to, and no threshold comparison anywhere in ORYN would surface that.

requirement_text: Grades or scores are valid for a maximum period of two years prior to the date of registration.
limitations: RECENCY RULE anchored to 'the date of registration' - a fifth distinct anchor phrasing in this corpus, after 'prior to entry' (Edinburgh), 'starting your course' (Bath), 'the first day of your course' (Liverpool), 'the start date of your course' (QMUL/Southampton) and 'the date the exam was taken' (Hacettepe, which anchors at the other end entirely).
researcher_notes: Seven institutions in this batch carry a recency rule and no two phrase the anchor identically. Registration and course start are not the same day at most universities, so the phrasings are not interchangeable even though they look it.

program_name: Medicine; Nursing; Midwifery; Physiotherapy; Veterinary Medicine
requirement_text: IELTS 7.5 with no less than 7.0 in any element
limitations: Subject to the REQ-9402 recency rule.
researcher_notes: The highest English threshold in this corpus. Nottingham's healthcare bar sits a full 1.5 bands above its foundation bar (REQ-9405) - the intra-institution spread on one test is wider than most inter-institution differences, which is why a single per-university English number is never right.

requirement_text: IELTS 6.0 with no less than 5.5 in any element
limitations: Applies to integrated foundation courses, NOT to standard three-year undergraduate degrees, whose thresholds are published per course rather than in this policy.

requirement_text: IELTS 5.5 with no less than 5.0 in any element
PTE entry requirement for foundation programmes is: an overall score of at least 59 and with no less than 53 in any element
The academic version of the IELTS
limitations: POSSIBLE ABSENCE, FLAGGED NOT ASSERTED. The extraction of this policy returned IELTS, PTE and the university's own pre-sessional course as the accepted routes and reported that TOEFL iBT is not mentioned anywhere in the document. If that is correct, Nottingham accepts no TOEFL at all, which would be a significant exclusion for US-curriculum applicants. But an extraction reporting an absence is weaker evidence than a quotation, and this lane does not convert 'not seen' into 'not accepted'. Re-read the rendered policy before recording a TOEFL exclusion for Nottingham.
researcher_notes: Recorded at medium confidence precisely so the open question survives instead of being silently dropped or silently upgraded.

requirement_text: 80 with no less than 21 in writing and at least 18 in every other section for tests taken before 21 January 2026.
source_authority_note: tudublin.ie has no .edu/.ac./.gov suffix and so is rejected by looksOfficial() in lib/acquisition/source-authority.ts, exactly as tcd.ie is. This is TU Dublin's own site publishing its own entry requirements. Needs institution official-domain provenance, piece (A) in source-authority-gap.md.
limitations: TOEFL iBT legacy 0-120/0-30 scales, correctly bounded to tests taken before the ETS rescale. Unambiguous because REQ-9411 supplies the other side. Expires for practical purposes in January 2028 when ETS ends comparable 0-120 reporting.
researcher_notes: Fourth institution found handling the rescale correctly, after Bath, Exeter and QMUL - and the first outside the UK.

requirement_text: For tests taken on/after 21 January 2026, the requirements are a total score of 4.5, with no less than 4.5 in writing and at least 4 in every other section
researcher_notes: Post-cutover 1-6 band scale, correctly applied. Compare directly with Edinburgh's already-recorded '4.5 with at least 4.0 in each component' - two institutions in two countries independently arriving at the same 1-6 figures, which is corroborating evidence that Edinburgh's numbers were the correct reading of the new scale and Glasgow's were not.

requirement_text: Test results must be from a single sitting; applicants cannot combine the results of multiple tests.
limitations: EXCLUSION ON SCORE PROVENANCE. A student who reaches every component threshold across two sittings holds numbers that satisfy the rule component-by-component and is nonetheless ineligible. No threshold comparison can detect this without a sitting identifier on the stored score.
researcher_notes: Third institution stating a single-sitting rule, after Koc ('superscores are not accepted') and QMUL ('TOEFL's MyBest scores'). Three different wordings of the same constraint - superscore, MyBest, single sitting - which is why matching on vocabulary rather than on the underlying provenance concept would miss two of the three.

requirement_text: 6.0 with no less than 6 in each component
limitations: IELTS Academic. The overall and the per-component floor are the same figure, which is unusual and means there is no headroom for a weak section.
researcher_notes: Page adds 'unless otherwise stated' and warns that some programmes require higher, so this is a floor.

requirement_text: the certificate of your English language standard/test must have been issued within 2 years of the expected start of your course.
limitations: RECENCY RULE anchored to 'the expected start of your course', and note it binds the ISSUE date of the certificate rather than the test date - a distinction that matters when a result is reissued.
researcher_notes: Sixth anchor phrasing in the corpus.

requirement_text: Applicants must be 18 before 31st December (September Start programmes) or 31st May (January Start programmes)
limitations: AN AGE BAR, expressed as two bare day-and-month cut-offs with no year - the same year-less shape as a recurring deadline, but attached to a requirement rather than a date. Evaluating it needs the student's birth date; ORYN deliberately stores birth YEAR only (spec Phase 2: 'Do not unnecessarily expose full birth date if birth year is sufficient'). For students born in the second half of the year the birth year alone cannot decide this, so the honest answer is needs_manual_review, not met.
researcher_notes: The single most product-relevant requirement in this batch. ORYN's declared users are 14-18; this rule excludes a meaningful slice of them from an institution ORYN already lists programmes for, and it is a genuine tension between the minor-safe data-minimisation principle and the requirement-check feature. Worth a product decision rather than a schema change: surface the rule and let the student answer, rather than storing a birth date to evaluate it silently.
